payload.answer: Implementation-ready specification with acceptance criteria. Small, well-bounded command; the design work is in the in-flight-jobs question and the interaction with CANCELLED, not in the transition itself.

Operators running vibey locally and, once the kopf operator lands, the operator reconciling a VibeyProject whose CR has been deleted. Both need the same service, not two code paths -- runbook 05 names that as a real risk.

Add `vibey abandon <project_id>`: transition a project to the ABANDONED phase, releasing its repo_path so a new project can be created against that repository. This is not hypothetical -- it is currently blocking real work. The project table has a `project_repo_uniq` constraint (one project per repo_path), and a stale project (expansion-13-cost-performance, stuck in BUILD since 2026-08-20, whose work actually shipped as PR #70) permanently holds [path] `vibey new --repo [path]` fails with UniqueViolationError and there is no supported way to release it. The only current escape is hand-editing the database, which is exactly what a CLI should prevent. ABANDONED is already a legal value in the Phase enum, so this finishes an existing concept rather than inventing one.

[hard] The ledger is append-only: abandoning is a recorded phase transition emitting an event, never a delete or an update-in-place of history. [hard] Go through the same application service the CLI and the operator both call -- a single choke point. [hard] Decide and implement what happens to the project's in-flight work: jobs in ready/leased/awaiting_human must not be left claimable, or a worker will keep picking up work for an abandoned project. Cancelling them is the natural answer, and CANCELLED is currently a dead enum value never written by anything -- but note the job-lifecycle-commands project is separately defining stop/restart semantics over that same state, so coordinate rather than inventing a conflicting meaning. [hard] Idempotent: abandoning an already-abandoned project succeeds quietly rather than erroring. [hard] Refuse to abandon a DONE project silently -- require confirmation or a flag, since DONE carries evidence. [hard] 100% branch coverage, domain purity, Conventional Commits, feature branch into develop.

payload.answer: Two beyond DONE. (1) Refuse by default if the project has LEASED jobs, because a live worker is mid-session and abandoning underneath it races the lease -- require an explicit --force and say in the message which jobs are leased. (2) Warn, but do not block, on unanswered human gates: abandoning is often precisely how you resolve a project parked on a question nobody will answer. Otherwise no friction; this is an operator cleaning up stuck state, and a command that argues is a command people route around with SQL.

`vibey new --repo <same path>` succeeds immediately afterwards. The project reads as ABANDONED in `vibey status`. A ledger event records the transition with who and when. No job for that project is left in a claimable state. Running abandon twice is a quiet no-op. Branches, PRs and worktree directories are all still present on disk and on GitHub.

Leave everything intact and delete nothing. Branches and PRs are evidence and may be the only record of what the run produced -- an abandon command that removes them converts a tidy-up into data loss. Warn if a worktree directory still exists, and print its path so the operator can remove it deliberately, but never remove it automatically: vibey's worktrees are real git worktrees and deleting one out from under a live worker is a corruption, not a cleanup.

When a project is wedged or its work already shipped by another route, I want to release its repo_path claim so I can start a new project in that repository -- without hand-editing Postgres. Live example: expansion-13-cost-performance has held [path] in BUILD since 2026-08-20 while its actual work merged as PR #70, and every `vibey new --repo [path]` since has failed on project_repo_uniq. The outcome I need is that the next `vibey new` succeeds.

payload.answer: Treat them differently, because they differ in whether anything is running. READY and AWAITING_HUMAN are inert: transition straight to CANCELLED, no race, no worker to consider. AWAITING_CAPACITY likewise. LEASED is the only hard one -- a live worker holds it and may be minutes into a paid session. Do not yank the row out from under it. Behind --force, mark the intent and let the lease drain, exactly as the SIGTERM drain already does for scale-in: the worker finishes the job in hand and claims no more. Without --force, refuse and name the leased jobs. SUCCEEDED and FAILED are terminal history and must not be rewritten -- the ledger is append-only, and retroactively cancelling a job that already succeeded would falsify the record.

Proceed independently on TIMING, but not on MEANING. Blocking this project until job-lifecycle-commands lands would stall a fix that is currently blocking real work, so build now. But do not define a private CANCELLED: the state has exactly one meaning -- this job will not run again -- and what differs is only how it got there. Record that as provenance on the transition event (abandoned_with_project versus a direct operator stop), never as a second flavour of the state. The test that keeps the two honest is that a CANCELLED job is not claimable regardless of which path produced it. If job-lifecycle-commands later adds a state machine in domain/, this code should move onto it rather than keep a parallel implementation -- say so in the PR so the follow-up is visible instead of forgotten.
